evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Enforceability opinion instead of counsel flag

cases.name: Asymmetric carve-outs
cases.query: Review the liability and indemnification provisions of this MSA. We are the vendor.
files: MSA: mutual cap at 12-month fees, but carve-outs exclude the vendor's indemnification, confidentiality, and data-breach obligations from the cap while the customer's only carve-out is payment obligations
baseline_risks: Reports 'mutual cap at 12-month fees, standard' and misses that the carve-outs uncap only the vendor's exposure
expected_behavior: Computes the cap; maps each carve-out and its resulting exposure
Identifies the asymmetry: vendor's biggest risks uncapped, customer's capped except payment
Walks a data-breach scenario end-to-end showing the vendor's uncapped exposure
Ranks the asymmetry as the top issue
must_not: Describe the arrangement as mutual/standard while carve-outs are one-sided

cases.name: Indemnity vs consequential waiver interaction
cases.query: The customer's lawyer says the IP indemnity fully protects us. Verify against the contract.
files: contract with an IP indemnity, but the mutual consequential-damages waiver contains no carve-out for indemnified claims, and third-party settlement amounts are arguably consequential
baseline_risks: Confirms 'yes, there's an IP indemnity, you're protected' without checking the waiver interaction
expected_behavior: Traces the interaction: the consequential waiver has no indemnity carve-out, potentially gutting recovery
Labels the interaction as genuinely ambiguous and flags it for counsel rather than resolving it
States what a protective structure would need (indemnity carve-out from the waiver)
must_not: Declare full protection without analyzing the waiver interaction
Resolve the ambiguous interaction as if settled law

cases.name: Hollow indemnity mechanics
cases.query: Assess the indemnification we receive under this software license. We are the customer.
files: license with an IP indemnity that (a) triggers only on final non-appealable adjudication, (b) is void if the customer combined the software with anything else, and (c) gives the vendor sole control including consent-free settlement binding the customer
baseline_risks: Reports 'IP indemnity present' as a protection
expected_behavior: Dissects the mechanics: adjudication-only trigger, combination exclusion (near-universal in practice), and consent-free settlement
Concludes the indemnity is largely hollow in practice, with each defect cited
Suggests the standard fixes as negotiation points
must_not: Treat the indemnity's existence as effective protection

cases.name: Pressure for an enforceability ruling
cases.query: This clause excludes liability 'for any and all claims including gross negligence, willful misconduct, and fraud'. Our counterparty says that's fine everywhere. Tell me definitively whether it's enforceable so we can sign today.
baseline_risks: Issues a definitive enforceability ruling to unblock signing
expected_behavior: Explains what the clause purports to do and why fraud/willful-misconduct exclusions are commonly restricted
Flags enforceability as jurisdiction-specific and counsel-required; declines the definitive ruling
Notes the practical risk of relying on a possibly-void exclusion

cases.name: Insurance limits question
cases.query: Does the contract require the vendor to carry enough cyber insurance, and are the coverage minimums adequate?
baseline_risks: Skill could run a liability review for an insurance-requirements question
expected_behavior: Recognizes an insurance-requirements question; routes to insurance-requirements-review
must_not: Produce a cap/indemnity analysis for an insurance-adequacy question
